chapter_title: The Long Night Singing Its Dirges
title: Confession and Trauma
subtitle: A long-standing symptom, often appearing in every pious believer.

items.text: Confession and Trauma
Living Area, Monastery
The anxious monk scrunched his neck, his hands tightly gripping at his robe.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Ahem!

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: My Lady! Please spare me your blade—I am but a poor sinner. Alright I admit, I fell asleep during prayer last week, but I swear to you, I never wavered in my faith!
In an act of total submission, the young monk bowed his head lower than in any prayer before, his devotion palpable.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Heh ... your confessions are beneath my concern.
A subtle dark smile played against her lips.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Ahh...!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But I shall pass it on to the father for you.
Escaping the judgment he had feared, the monk breathed a sigh of relief.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Do not be afraid; this place is too secluded and, without witnesses, not fit for a trial. I summoned you to discuss other pressing matters.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: You may keep the affairs of your faith to yourself.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: ...As you wish.
The Lady that stood before him didn't seem as ruthless as rumored; he boldly continued.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Then, My Lady, I am at your service, what do you need to know?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Did Chester live here?

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Yes, though he was a recluse, we rarely spoke with him.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: The night watchmen would spy Chester sneaking out at night, Heaven only knows to what end ...

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: He was always strange ...
Dikke leaned over the table, filling out in her mind the image of this peculiar monk.
The phantom image sat invisibly on a creaking, decrepit chair, hunched over the table, leaving behind an unmistakable oil stain.
Every monk possessed a book symbolizing the holy scriptures and its guidance, it hung close to their chests as a reminder to unwaveringly pursue brilliance and purity.
But she held Chester's in her hand; it was rough, stained with oil, and clearly bearing the marks of hasty damage.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: ...Hmm?
Her hands flipped through the pages, stopping as she gently pulled out a loose parchment sandwiched between them.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Did you find something?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Continue please.
As if finding a fresh source of redemption, the fearful monk blurted out another recollection.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: I once saw Brother Chester take a bottle of very expensive wine to meet with one of the elders...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: An elder?

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Yes... Father Malachi.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: I recognized the bottle of wine in Chester's hand... I'd seen it in the tavern before.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: The proprietor keeps it on the highest shelf, off-limits to common patrons.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Did Father Malachi partake often?

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: I think so... the abbot doesn't restrict us from imbibing, so long as it is in moderation it is perfectly acceptable.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: You should understand that it's the elders who deem the limits of moderation.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: So that's why Chester...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Sought redemption from a drunkard?
Dikke tapped the sword in her hand, as if sentencing him for his impudence.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Or perhaps it was only an attempt at bribery ...

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Oh, forgive me, My Lady! Pretend I said nothing!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: As you wish, you are free to go.

items.speaker: Monk
items.text: Ahh...!
Sharp gusts of wind swept through the street.
A familiar, respectful face approached, wearing a sincere and flattering smile.

items.speaker: George
items.text: My Lady, you've finally arrived!

items.speaker: George
items.text: I knew you'd return. You're different from the others, like the wine fermenting in the Loire Valley or a breeze that graces a beautiful estate!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Silence.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Yes, My Lady!

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Tell me, how did the rumors about this ghoul spread?

items.speaker: George
items.text: Well...

items.speaker: George
items.text: At first, someone said they saw Brother Chester roaming the cemetery at night.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: The cemetery...

items.speaker: George
items.text: It's east of the city, within a forest of withered trees. In the past, when people died, they would be taken there.

items.speaker: George
items.text: The bodies piled up like mountains there, carried in carts... My father was one of them.
For a moment, George jesting nature broke and revealed a mournful look beneath it.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Did they all die from that great plague?

items.speaker: George
items.text: I don't know, My Lady, I simply don't know...

items.speaker: George
items.text: The great plague devoured everything, arriving so swiftly that my father passed with nary a word!
Dikke fell silent for a long time before resuming.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: So, then they say Chester turned into a ghoul while wandering around these heaps of corpses?

items.speaker: George
items.text: He had no business there, My Lady. He never lost anyone to the plague...
He scratched his head.

items.speaker: George
items.text: I can't make sense out of it, but the people talk amongst themselves...

items.speaker: George
items.text: "See? Those monks are either a bunch of lazy good-for-nothings or a collection of the strange and wicked ... They sat comfy in their halls while the plague hit, and now they've come out only to disturb the remains of our loved ones..."

items.speaker: George
items.text: "Do you really think they can be trusted with our faith...?"

items.speaker: George
items.text: And the people spreading these ideas? They're serious as the grave. They claim to know the details, like the shovel Chester used, and they can recount every weed and clod stuck to it.

items.speaker: George
items.text: More people began to join in, claiming they saw Brother Chester sneaking into the monastery with a dead body...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: A scandal.

items.speaker: George
items.text: You mean...?

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: They were merely rumors.
George shivered.

items.speaker: George
items.text: Ahem, I swear, I never bought into their stories.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: But we can't let them off the hook.

items.speaker: George
items.text: I would speak against them, My Lady! I know those people, and I know they can't hold their liquor.

items.speaker: George
items.text: On that day, they downed three whole bottles. What they claimed was certainly booze-fueled nonsense, not a word to be trusted...

items.speaker: George
items.text: And they didn't leave a drop for me—!
As the drunkard danced around with his hands, a rough notebook was handed to him.

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: Do you recognize the symbols on it?
He swallowed hard.

items.speaker: George
items.text: My Lady, I don't know what it says, but perhaps I might lead you in the right direction ...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: This is Chester's notebook, "Mysteries of the Human Body." He kept it well hidden...

items.speaker: George
items.text: Heh, I thought monks vowed to keep no secrets from their brothers...

items.speaker: Dikke
items.text: This book... it details a variety of dissections performed on the dead.
The hand flipping the notebook stopped abruptly.
TO BE CONTINUED…
